messages.author: 1ce64fad997d9303
messages.subject: dNmixture_*() use with missing counts
parts:
Hi all,

I would love to use the dNmixture_*() distributions. I'm analyzing "citizen science" data, though, so I have around 700 sites with up to 9 surveys, but some of those sites completed only as few as 4 surveys.

Is there a straightforward way of handling this sort of missing data using the dNmixture_*() distributions? Passing the data as a 700 x 9 matrix (that I call "C") with missing counts as NAs does not seem to work automatically.

I know I have to loop through sites and provide all surveys to dNmixture_s() as C[i,1:nsurveys], which is the complicating factor because will be NAs in there. I have some ideas that might get around this (e.g., dynamic indexing perhaps), but nothing straightforward given the irregular data. I just want to make sure there isn't something on the nimble side of things to facilitate this, like an `na.rm = T` option.

Thank you,
Gates

messages.author: 2e52e6a395617594
messages.subject: Re: dNmixture_*() use with missing counts

You could try passing your observations as a vector rather than a matrix, removing the missing counts. Mason Fidino had a nice blog post on this: https://masonfidino.com/nested_indexing/

Adrian

messages.subject: Re: dNmixture_*() use with missing counts
parts:
Thanks for this, Adrian!

Follow-up question. Playing around with this today. It seems `dNmixture_s()` expects the observation data (here, C) to be in the form of, generally: C[site, first_count:last_count]

I'm trying to use `dNmixture_s()` for a multi-year multi-species model, though. So, for species `b` in year `t`, the right-hand side would look like:

dNmixture_s(
      lambda = lambda[t,b],
      prob = p[t,b],
      Nmin = 0, Nmax = 500,
      len = length_survey[n])

I don't know exactly what the left-hand side should look like. I tried C[b, first_count:last_count], but got the "multiple definitions for node(s)" error for all C[,] values.

Should I instead us C[site, first_count:last_count] and have nested species indexes for first_count:last_count that I would then use for `lambda` and `prob` too? Or something else?

I can share some reproducible code if it would help. Haven't yet found a multi-species or multi-year example for the dNmixture distributions, would love to see one if it's out there.

Thank you!
Gates

messages.subject: Re: dNmixture_*() use with missing counts
parts:
Hi John, 

Many thanks for this. Glad to hear dNmix should be able to handle additional indexing -- I'm working on a simulated example now to get a feel for it. As for the error message, my impression was that the error was pointing out that I wasn't specifying a site for each set of repeated surveys. Could that be the case?

My inferential objective is estimating overall expected abundance (lambda), and I'm not (yet) exploring site-level variation, so lambda and p aren't varying across sites. There are 16 species, 33 years, and over 700 sites, so the model already takes 4 days to run without including site-level effects, which is becoming a bit prohibitive. So that's why I don't think the indexing of lambda and p would be the issue -- maybe that makes sense?

Thanks again!
Gates

parts:
As an update... I've created a data object (C) as a 4D array with the structure: C[n_sites, n_visits, n_years, n_species], where NA values are moved to the tail of each row of C, which allows me to have another matrix for the length of each survey to feed to dNmix. 

However, since not every site reports every year, I have some rows of C that are entirely NA, such that the survey length is then 0. That will not work with dNmix because 1:surv_length[i] will become 1:0 and that will give in error. Although there are over 200,000 observations, the amount of "missing data" under the 4D format is 90%, which is substantial.

Back to the drawing board! I think I will need to convert back to the nested indexing idea. Still open to any suggestions. Thank you!

Best,
Gates

parts:
Hi Gates--

Indexing is definitely a hassle as models get bigger, so I totally understand the headache.

Thanks for sending along reproducible code. I was able to diagnose the "multiple definitions" error. You're looping over nsurveys and using dynamic indexing to extract observations for each species based on a start and end vector. All of the model code looks fine. The issue appears to be that "start_obs" and "end_obs" contain duplicates, such that as you loop through surveys, you're going back over your start/end. For example, survey 1 is associated with obs 1-4, but survey 42 is associated with obs 1-5. Maybe you're trying to have different values for each species? In that case, you could make start_obs and end_obs matrices.

Hope this helps. In general, I always find dynamic indexing easiest if the data are as "long form" as possible, with columns I can use to dynamically index parameters, groups, etc. You seem to be going down that track.

Ben
